name: Warp
look: Warm brown-dark canvas, off-white as the only 'colour', very tight 3–4px radii, terminal mockups as the whole decorative system.

hero.title: The terminal, reconsidered
hero.sub: Blocks instead of a scrollback soup. A real text editor on the command line. Command history that is searchable, shareable and actually yours.

features.title: A terminal that keeps its shape
features.sub: Everything here exists because a scrollback buffer is a bad interface for work you need to come back to.

items.title: Blocks, not scrollback
items.body: Every command and its output is one addressable block you can collapse, copy, re-run, bookmark or share as a link.

items.title: A real editor
items.body: Selection, multiple cursors, undo and find — on the command line, behaving the way they do everywhere else.

items.title: History that is searchable
items.body: Fuzzy search across every command you have run, scoped by directory, with the working directory and exit code attached.

items.title: Shared sessions
items.body: Send a colleague a link to a live session or a single block. They see the command, the output and the environment it ran in.

items.title: Written in Rust
items.body: GPU-accelerated rendering, under 40ms from keystroke to frame, on a hundred thousand lines of output.

items.title: Workflows
items.body: Save a parameterised command with a description, then find it by what it does rather than by remembering its flags.

showcases.title: Every command is an object
showcases.body: Output stops being an undifferentiated stream. A block knows which command produced it, in which directory, with which exit code — so you can fold it, re-run it, or send someone a permalink to the failure.
points: Collapse, copy or re-run any block
Permalink a single block to a colleague

showcases.title: Runbooks that live in the terminal
showcases.body: Save the commands your team actually runs as workflows with descriptions and named parameters. New starters find them by searching for the task, not by grepping a wiki nobody has updated since the migration.

metric_lead: Measured on a 2024 laptop against 100,000 lines of output

items.q: Does it work with my shell?
items.a: Yes — zsh, bash and fish, with your existing configuration, aliases and prompt left alone. Relay adds a layer above the shell rather than replacing it.

items.q: Does my command history leave my machine?
items.a: Only if you turn on cloud sync, which is off by default. With it off, history is stored locally and nothing is transmitted.
Yes, as of 2.0, on x86_64 and arm64 with packages for Debian, Fedora and Arch. Windows is in beta.
Blocks and history work on the remote host once the lightweight helper is installed there; without it you get a standard terminal session with local blocks only.

cta.title: Try it for an afternoon
cta.sub: Free for individuals, on macOS, Linux and Windows. Your shell config carries over.

footer.tagline: A terminal built for how people actually work in one.

notes: The only 'colour' in the system is an off-white that doubles as body text on the canvas and as the primary button fill. There is no chromatic brand accent.
The canvas is warm brown-dark, not black. That warmth is the brand — every neutral, including dividers and body text, carries a hint of it.
Button radii are extremely tight at 3–4px. Pills are reserved for icon containers and nothing else.
Inter with DM Mono is the canonical pairing; Instrument Serif appears only as an occasional editorial italic.
Terminal mockups are the entire decorative system. No gradients, no atmospheric overlays, no illustration.
